title: HEATER, BLOWER & RESISTOR ASM.
summary: Heater box installation (all models): the heater & blower assembly (blower motor housing, engine side of the firewall) and the heater & defroster assembly (heater box under the dash) clamp the dash panel (firewall) between them, held by nuts on studs; the blower flange is sealed with 55a sealer. A duct is screwed to the heater box, a seal goes around the heater core pipes, and the blower motor resistor is screwed in with its harness plug (View A).

parts.name: HEATER & BLOWER ASM.
parts.name_expanded: Heater & blower assembly – blower motor housing (engine side of firewall)

parts.name: SPL. WASHER
parts.name_expanded: Special washer – on heater case studs at the dash panel

parts.name: HEATER & DEF ASM.
parts.name_expanded: Heater & defroster assembly – heater box (passenger side, under dash)

materials.where: flange of heater & blower asm. [1] where it meets the dash panel

fastening.note: Nuts [7] (5 shown) go on from the engine side onto studs, through the flange of the blower housing [1] and the dash panel; the studs line up with the heater & def asm. [4] behind the dash.
Special washers [2] (3 shown) sit on the studs of [4] between the heater case and the dash panel opening; the drawing does not show separate fasteners for them.
Sealer 55a bead along the blower housing [1] flange against the dash panel; bead at least .38 dia. measured perpendicular to the flange when applied.
Seal [3] fits around the heater core pipes where they come through the dash panel.
Screw [5] holds the duct [6] to the lower end of the heater box [4].
View A: screw [9] goes through the resistor [8] plate into the case (two holes in the plate, one screw drawn); the wiring harness plug (see UPC 12) pushes onto the resistor terminals.

notes: NOTE: At time of application, sealer bead must be .38 dia minimum-measured perpendicular to flange.
